summary: Tested NEW AEC Hindi Grammar course feature + full regression on existing SEC course. Backend: 18/18 new AEC-specific pytest tests passing + full suite 56/56 (100%) including all 3 other AEC sample topics scoring 100% on all-correct submit, and a global uniqueness check across all 457 AEC MCQ ids (no duplicate-id bug, unlike the previously-fixed SEC issue). Frontend: AEC tab renders stats (25 topics, 457 questions) and 2 unit-grouped lists (13+12) correctly; opened 3 topics (sandhi, muhavare, nibandh-paryavaran) - all rich content blocks (definition box, table, paragraphs, CTA) rendered correctly with proper Hindi text; completed a full 7-question quiz for nibandh-paryavaran via the shared quiz engine, got accurate 29% (2/7) matching the actual picks made (no scoring corruption) and landed on quiz-result screen correctly; returned to dashboard, SEC tab/chapters/progress-rings/daily-practice-card all rendered and worked normally (regression pass). Rapid SEC<->AEC tab switching (6 cycles) produced no crash and no stale data mixing - re-opening AEC tab after visiting a SEC chapter screen still showed correct AEC data.
critical_code_review_comments: AEC MCQ ids use a global incrementing numeric suffix format 'mcq-it-course-app-{n}' (confirmed via sample fetch) which avoids the earlier per-chapter-counter collision bug class entirely - good design choice reusing a single shared counter at content-generation time rather than per-chapter.

server.py AEC seeding on startup uses idempotent upsert (update_one with upsert=True) for both aec_topics and the shared mcqs collection - correctly avoids the non-idempotent count==0 seeding bug pattern that caused the SEC duplicate-id issue previously.
/api/aec/stats computes mcqs by excluding SEC chapter ids + 'daily' via $nin - this is correct but slightly fragile if a future chapter_id collides with an AEC slug; low risk, no action needed now.
dashboard.tsx correctly resets courseTab state to default 'sec' on remount (e.g. navigating away and back) rather than persisting AEC tab choice - acceptable default behavior, not a bug.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_aec_course.py (new file: 18 tests covering /api/aec/topics, /api/aec/topics/{slug}, /api/aec/syllabus, /api/aec/stats, shared quiz engine mcq-id-uniqueness + 100% scoring for sandhi + 4 other sampled topics, global 457-mcq uniqueness check, and SEC /api/chapters regression check)

success_rate.frontend: 100% for all tested flows: AEC tab stats/list rendering, 3 topic detail screens (rich content blocks), full quiz completion + accurate scoring + result screen, SEC regression (chapters/progress rings/daily practice), rapid tab-switch stress test (no crash, no stale data)

seed_data_creation: None persisted beyond normal guest quiz-result documents created during testing (guest tokens, no PII, not cleaned up as these are anonymous user data consistent with app design).
context_for_next_testing_agent: AEC Hindi Grammar course feature is fully working end-to-end on both backend and frontend with zero regressions found on the existing SEC course. All known-passing features (admin login, guest access, SEC study material/quiz/daily-practice/progress-rings/bookmarks) remain intact after light regression checks. No further action needed for this feature; safe to ship.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no new bugs found in this iteration. The duplicate-mcq-id bug class previously seen on the SEC course does NOT reproduce on AEC because AEC MCQ ids are generated with a distinct, globally-unique string format at content-authoring time rather than a per-chapter runtime counter, and seeding uses idempotent update_one upserts.
